title: #111893 Add Warnings For Missing Index Templates

timeline.body:
Fixes [ES#111893 - Data stream restoration/promotion without a matching template](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/111893)

This PR adds warnings headers and log messages for the following conditions:

* Promoting a CCR replicated data stream wihout a matching index template for the data stream
* Restoring a snapshot of a data stream without a matching index template for the data stream

In both these senarios, the action will succede however future rollovers of the data stream will fail due to the missing templates. By adding a warning header and log, we make the user explicitly aware of this pending failure.

Documentation for both these actions has also been updated to warn of this scenario

Documentation preview:

I was trying to ensure there was no chance overlapping templates from the test setup could give a false fail if there was some overlap on the patterns but you're right, in this case it's overkill. Have remove the delete of `with-fs` data stream and the corresponding template.

Though I do still need to delete `other-ds` as it's covered by TEMPLATE_1 and I can't delete the template while a matching DS is still there.

timeline.body:
If I understand this correctly, this code checks only the current cluster state for a matching template while the template could be restored as part of the snapshot. Should we consider checking the `metadataBuilder` or the `globalMetadata`, that are set here: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a59c182f9f7e9d1bf3d6eecbc0e44f24ff91d053/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/snapshots/RestoreService.java#L347-L349

This should be verified, I haven't tested it, but I think it might be a valid scenario.

reply.body:
I think you are right... There might be a few failed rollover attempts while the restore is in progress (if the DS gets restored before the templates) but I believe it would rollover successfully in the end so it's a valid scenario and should not warn.

I'll get that logic in and add some tests for these senario.

Logic and tests added however the test is affected by https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/107515 so I have had to mute it :-/ I did some manual runs of the test with `org/elasticsearch/test/ESIntegTestCase.java:1305` commented out to prevent the cluster state size mismatch failing the test and it all passed.

The comment reffers to the "step" of these test as a whole rather than that line specifically so perhaps:

```suggestion
            // Prepare index template request and execute
```

It's ok, you can leave it as is. I think my initial confusion is that this request is sent to both clusters but the execution for the leader cluster was a few lines later, but it's not far enough to warrant a more specific comment.

timeline.body: Why are we also trying to clean up the individual backing indices? Is cleaning up the data stream not enough?

reply.body:
I must admit I copied this from the cleanup step of another test the creates and promotes DataStreams in this class so I'm assuming the original author had their reasons which can be a dangerous thing to do 😅 

I think possibly this ensures the indices are cleaned up, even if the data stream gets itself into into a corrupted state during the test and doing the cleanup prevents other tests in the suite then failing?

We all have done that :). 

Unfortunately, I also cannot say with confidence that this can never happen. 

I have to admit that I do find this way of "tear down" a bit unusual. I would prefer to have a tear down method that would wipe the cluster at the end of every test so we do not have to deal with this but I do understand that this is out of the scope of this. 

So, happy to keep this, but maybe add a comment, that we do not know if this is necessary but we do it to be sure? So, at least the next maintainer can factor this in. What do you think?
